newsitem.title: USA: Crown Central sued over Houston refinery emissions.
newsitem.headline: Crown Central sued over Houston refinery emissions.

text.p: An environmental group Monday sued Crown Central Petroleum Corp., seeking to force the oil company to comply with federal and state emissions standards at its Pasadena, Texas, refinery.
The lawsuit alleges the company's 100,000 barrel-a-day refinery exceeded allowable hydrogen sulfide and sulphur dioxide emissions limits for more than 10,000 hours between May 1992 and December 1996.

The Texas Natural Resources Conservation Commission on July 10 cited Crown for alleged emissions violations, but the environmental groups said the Texas regulators have done little to enforce clean-air regulations at the refinery.

"TNRCC has done little more than periodically rattle its sabre at Crown. Each time, Crown gets off with either a warning or a modest penalty, and it keeps polluting," Neil Carmen of the Sierra Club said.

An industry source told Reuters it was likely the commission would take formal enforcement action on the latest series of allegations, which could lead to an order to clean up operations and fines for each emissions violation.

Randall Trembly, executive vice president for the Baltimore-based company, said Crown met with the environmental groups before the federal lawsuit was filed to discuss its plans to upgrade equipment and reduce emissions.
"The company plans to vigorously defend the lawsuit," he said in a statement.

Crown's Pasadena refinery has been operated by managers and contractors since February 1996, when union workers were locked out over a contract dispute. The company also has been sued by refinery workers alleging racial and sexual discrimination, and by Pasadena residents seeking $50 million in punitive damages for pollution from the refinery.

The latest lawsuit was filed by Washington-based Trial Lawyers for Public Justice on behalf of Texans United for a Safe Economy Educational Fund and three of its members, along with the Natural Resources Defence Counsel and Sierra Club.
